newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Springbok rugby coach Andre Markgraaff will be axed if it can be proved that it was his voice uttering racist remarks on the tape recording broadcast on television news on Monday night.

- Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo is to be summoned to the parliamentary finance committee to explain why government should accede to the Post Ofice's request for 213 million rand when the parastatal was scheduled to become profitable this year.

- Harmony, the Randgold-managed Free State mine, is poised to become one of South Africa's largest gold producers in terms of a proposed deal to buy stablemate Grootvlei and nearby Consolidated Modderfontein for about 250 million rand.

- Industrial holdings group T&N Holdings saw attributable income crash 46 percent to 22.1 million rand for the year to December as the motor industry development programme bit into original equipment sales and internal problems hit the friction division.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Rainbow Chicken 's management was accused by the Food and Allied Workers' Union (Fawu) on Monday of not being serious about saving the troubled broiler producer.
- A major restructuring of NBS Holdings' executive management is underway in the wake of the NBS Boland Bank merger and last week's severing of the cross- shareholding with Norwich.

- South African Airways SAA.CN has plans to buy an equity stake in SA Airlink, a local passenger service airline, a source said on Monday at the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the two airlines and SA Express.

- Grinaker Construction, the unbundled company hived off from Anglovaal's Grinaker Holdings, beat most of the construction sector on Monday when it reported a 69-percent rise in earnings on a 20-percent rise in turnover for the six months ended December 31.
SAKE BEELD
- The South African Post Office is heading for a big crisis since its loss of about 213 million rand and urgent steps are required to save the situation.
- President Nelson Mandela on Monday repudiated a special tax amnesty for blacks.

- About twenty construction companies in Gauteng were seriously affected on Monday by the Construction of Allied Workers Union (Cawu) strike about a loan dispute that affects only about seven percent of the workers.
THE STAR
- Andre Markgraaff could be axed as Springbok coach amid allegations on Monday night that he is the official who allegedly made taped racist remarks.

- Malawian police and South African expatriates were confident of a breakthrough early today in busting the gang of kidnappers who abducted Timothy Funnell from his adoptive parents' home on Saturday.
- Tensions are rising between ANC branches and their leaders in local government structures over the extent of the new councillors' independence from the party.
- A seven-month-pregnant woman and her unborn baby were killed during an attempted robbery at a Spar supermarket in Eastleigh, Edenvale, on Monday.
